intro: The Pythia has fallen silent at Delphi, and the pilgrims crowd the Sacred Way with questions no longer answered from the laurel-dark vapour. In her place she has left five riddles, each sworn upon a different god, their words carved as firmly as oaths into the temple's trembling stones. The suppliants wander from tripod to tripod, murmuring the verses to the bronze turnovers and the laurel leaves, hoping some hidden breath will turn them into guidance. Before they leave, every traveller presses a small stamped disk of his own mark into the base of the omphalos, as if to leave a part of his name with the silence. Night settles over the Castalian spring, and the unanswered press their ears to the stones, waiting for a meaning to gather itself out of the marks they have made.
echo: The journey home took ten years, and every long journey since has borrowed its name.
